read in ONE cycle,
single-port RAMs" style="text;html=1;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;fontSize=11;fontFamily=Helvetica;" vertex="1" parent="1"><mxGeometry x="960" y="362" width="190" height="52" as="geometry" /></mxCell><mxCell id="f1" value="WHY IT MATTERS: the gather needs src[k] and src[k+1] together for every output. Split by PARITY, one address into each bank gives both -- no dual-port RAM, no second read cycle. The 64-bit read and the parity split are the same decision." style="text;html=1;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;fontSize=11;fontFamily=Helvetica;" vertex="1" parent="1"><mxGeometry x="24" y="430" width="1130" height="56" as="geometry" /></mxCell><mxCell id="f2" value="MEASURED: pass 1 fell from 5.21 s to 3.74 s. The full-width read is part of that; the rest is on-fabric coefficient generation. Alignment is handled ONCE at the row base; nothing downstream of the bank write knows the row was ever misaligned." style="text;html=1;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;fontSize=10.5;fontFamily=Helvetica;" vertex="1" parent="1"><mxGeometry x="24" y="570" width="1130" height="40" as="geometry" /></mxCell></root></mxGraphModel></diagram></mxfile>
svg.text: A pulse row is N x 4 bytes with N ODD, so consecutive row bases alternate between 8-byte and 4-byte alignment. The bus is 64 bits.
correct, but HALF the bus idles
Alignment is a property of the ADDRESS, not the data. Narrowing every beat to fix the first one pays the cost on all 4319 of them.
CASE A IN_BASE[2] = 0 (rd_odd = 0) -- row starts on a beat boundary
CASE B IN_BASE[2] = 1 (rd_odd = 1) -- row starts MID-beat
read from IN_BASE & ~7 ar_size = 3'b011 (8 bytes) ALWAYS
and the two lanes land in different BANKS, by sample parity

WHY IT MATTERS: the gather needs src[k] and src[k+1] together for every output. Split by PARITY, one address into each bank gives both -- no dual-port RAM, no second read cycle. The 64-bit read and the parity split are the same decision.

MEASURED: pass 1 fell from 5.21 s to 3.74 s. The full-width read is part of that; the rest is on-fabric coefficient generation. The discarded word costs one beat per row -- 1 in 2160 for a 4319-sample row -- against the 2x the narrow path was giving up on every beat.
Source: sar_resample_v.v:627-696. Alignment is handled ONCE at the row base; nothing downstream of the bank write knows the row was ever misaligned.
